title: Cohomological boundedness of stratified dualizable condensed sheaves
statement: Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $B=p_Y^*\Lambda$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(B)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with ordinary relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $K\in D(B)$ admit a finite stratification of $Y$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-constructible-subset], on each of which its derived restriction is dualizable: there are an object $D$ and evaluation $D\otimes K\to B$ and coevaluation $B\to K\otimes D$ with the two contraction composites equal to the identities, using the usual associators and unitors [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Then there exist integers $a\le b$ such that $H^j(K)=0$ for $j<a$ and for $j>b$. In particular, $K$ has a cochain representative $C^\bullet$ with $C^j=0$ for every $j<a$. No Noetherian, finite-dimensional, or regularity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 4.11 and Lemma 4.10, with constructibility as in Definition 3.3

proof.text: Apply [lem-fix-constructible-open-closed-refinement] to the given finite constructible partition of $Y$. This gives a finite rooted binary tree, with root $Y$, every vertex qcqs, and each internal vertex split into a quasi-compact open subscheme and its closed complement. Each nonempty leaf $T$ has an actual morphism to one original stratum, compatible with its map to $Y$. By [lem-zl-condensed-lisse-proetale-locality], pullback along that morphism preserves the given dual pair. Thus $K_T$ is dualizable on each nonempty leaf. The restriction identifications use the inverse-image coefficient isomorphisms, not an extension of scalars to a different coefficient ring. Empty leaves have the zero module category and may be discarded.

source.place: Definition 3.3 and Corollary 4.11: finite-stratum reduction, made into a scheme-theoretic open/closed refinement tree

proof.text: Fix a nonempty leaf $T$. It is quasi-compact, so [det-pe-hypercover-single-cover], applied to the final object of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, supplies one covering map $u:W=\operatorname{Spec}D\to T$ with $D$ w-contractible. By [lem-zl-condensed-lisse-proetale-locality], $K_W=u^*K_T$ is dualizable. Put $A=\Gamma(W,B_W)$. Apply the equivalence of [lem-zl-condensed-wcontractible-lisse-evaluation]: there is a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finitely generated projective $A$-modules and an isomorphism $K_W\simeq F_W(P^\bullet)$, where $F_W(Q)=B_W\otimes^L_{\underline A}\underline Q$ is its exact symmetric monoidal scalar realization. Choose integers $a_T\le b_T$ outside which $P^\bullet$ vanishes (use $[0,0]$ for a zero model).

source.place: Lemma 4.10 proof, reduction to a w-contractible qcqs scheme; Lemma 4.1(2)

proof.text: For a term $P^r$, finite generation [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] gives a surjection $A^{m_r}\twoheadrightarrow P^r$. Projectivity [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] lifts $\mathrm{id}_{P^r}$ through this surjection, so $P^r[0]$ is a retract of $A^{m_r}[0]$. The exact symmetric monoidal $F_W$ of [lem-zl-condensed-wcontractible-lisse-evaluation] is additive, preserves this retraction and sends $A[0]$ to $B_W[0]$. Hence $F_W(P^r[0])$ is a retract of $B_W^{m_r}[0]$. Applying the cohomology functor [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to its two splitting maps makes its cohomology in degree $q\ne0$ a retract of zero; its identity is therefore zero. Thus each realized term is concentrated in degree zero.

source.place: Lemma 4.10 proof, bounded finite-projective model; elementary explanation for its realized terms

proof.text:
Write $P_{\ge r}$ for the brutal tail retaining the terms of $P$ in degrees at least $r$. For $a_T\le r\le b_T$ there is a degreewise split short exact sequence of complexes
$$0\to P_{\ge r+1}\to P_{\ge r}\to P^r[0][-r]\to0.$$
By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] it gives a distinguished triangle. The exact functor $F_W$ of [lem-zl-condensed-wcontractible-lisse-evaluation] preserves this triangle and its shifts. Descending induction on $r$ now proves that $F_W(P_{\ge r})$ has cohomology in $[r,b_T]$: the starting tail $P_{\ge b_T+1}$ is zero, the realized quotient is concentrated in degree $r$ by Step 3, and for $q<r$ or $q>b_T$ the two outer terms in
$$H^q(F_W(P_{\ge r+1}))\to H^q(F_W(P_{\ge r}))\to H^q(F_W(P^r[0])[-r])$$
vanish. Exactness is [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. At $r=a_T$ this proves $H^q(K_W)=0$ outside $[a_T,b_T]$. This uses preservation of triangles and finite free retracts; it does not assert t-exactness of scalar realization on arbitrary complexes.

source.place: Lemma 4.10 proof, bounded-projective amplitude argument, with the finite-tail induction written explicitly

proof.text: For any scheme morphism $f:S\to T$, [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] identifies $f^{-1}B_T$ with $B_S$. Thus its module inverse image is geometric inverse image with transported scalars, which is exact by [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact]. Applying it termwise computes derived restriction, and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $f^*H^q(L)\cong H^q(f^*L)$ for every complex $L$. In particular, for the singleton cover $u:W\to T$ in Step 2, $u^*H^q(K_T)=0$ outside $[a_T,b_T]$. Apply [lem-zl-condensed-cover-restriction-conservative] to the degree-zero derived object $H^q(K_T)[0]$: its restriction is zero, hence it is zero. Therefore $H^q(K_T)=0$ outside that interval on every nonempty leaf.

source.place: Lemma 4.10 proof: pro-etale restriction preserves the t-structure and is conservative; Stacks Tags 04JC and 010N for the exact-functor calculation

proof.text: If there are nonempty leaves, set $a=\min_T a_T$ and $b=\max_T b_T$; finiteness of the tree gives integers $a\le b$. If there are none, put $a=b=0$. Fix $q<a$ or $q>b$. On every leaf the restriction of $H^q(K)$ is zero, by Step 5 and its cohomology/restriction identification (and trivially on an empty leaf). Induct upward through the finite tree. At an internal vertex $V$ with closed child $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$ and quasi-compact open child $j:U\hookrightarrow V$, the sheaf $H^q(K_V)$ has inverse images $H^q(K_Z)=0$ and $H^q(K_U)=0$. All the hypotheses of [lem-exc-open-closed-detection] hold by Step 1, so $H^q(K_V)=0$. At the root this gives $H^q(K)=0$. The empty-root case is also covered. This proves the asserted uniform two-sided cohomological boundedness.

source.place: Corollary 4.11 proof, conservativity of open and closed restriction; finite-tree induction makes the finite-stratum induction explicit

proof.text: Take any cochain representative $E^\bullet$ of $K$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define $C^q=0$ for $q<a$, $C^a=\operatorname{coker}(d_E^{a-1})$, and $C^q=E^q$ for $q>a$, with the differential out of degree $a$ induced by $d_E^a$. This is the good lower truncation [def-kun-truncations]. The quotient map $E\to C$ is a chain map. Above $a$ it preserves cohomology, in degree $a$ its cohomology is $\ker(d_E^a)/\operatorname{im}(d_E^{a-1})$, and below $a$ both cohomologies vanish by Step 6. It is therefore a quasi-isomorphism and represents an isomorphism in $D(B)$. The resulting representative $C^\bullet$ is zero in every degree below $a$, as required.

source.place: Corollary 4.11, bounded-below representative consequence by good truncation

proof_origin.place: Definition 3.3, Lemma 4.1(2), Lemma 4.10 and Corollary 4.11; finite refinement, bounded-tail induction and good truncation written out
